title.en: History: Early Revolts against British Rule in Tamil Nadu

text.en: Raju saw a statue of a brave Tamil fighter. "Did the south revolt against the British?" he asked.

Before 1857, Tamil Nadu saw early revolts against the British East India Company. Pulithevar of Nerkattumseval fought against the Company's tax claims. Veerapandiya Kattabomman of Panchalankurichi refused to pay tax and was hanged in 1799.
Marudhu Brothers of Sivaganga led a revolt and issued the Tiruchirappalli Proclamation calling for unity against the British. Dheeran Chinnamalai of Kongu country fought with the support of Tipu Sultan's methods.
The Vellore Revolt of 1806 was a rising of Indian soldiers against changes in dress that hurt their religious feelings. Though crushed, these revolts showed early resistance.
